findings.summary: 3D computer graphics software converts a three-dimensional geometric model into a two-dimensional image through a pipeline of modeling, layout/animation, and rendering. Modeling constructs objects from polygonal vertices and faces. Layout positions and animates those objects within a virtual scene using keyframing or motion capture. Rendering calculates light transport and surface scattering to produce the final image, employing techniques such as ray tracing, rasterization, or path tracing to simulate shading, shadows, and optical effects.

mechanisms.title: Polygonal Modeling and Mesh Construction
mechanisms.explanation: Objects are formed from vertices that define polygons, typically triangles. The polygon structure determines model integrity and suitability for animation. Artists use modeling tools to create these meshes, which may also be generated by scanning or procedural methods.

mechanisms.title: Rendering Light Transport and Shading
mechanisms.explanation: Rendering simulates light transport and surface scattering to generate images. Techniques include ray tracing, rasterization, and path tracing, which compute shading, shadows, reflections, and other optical effects based on light placement and surface properties.
